messages.subject: Failed to Install INLA
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

When I run "install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)"
keeps me giving this error:

Warning in install.packages :
  downloaded length 37247792 != reported length 61470859
Warning in install.packages :
  URL 'https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable/bin/windows/contrib/4.2/INLA_22.05.07.zip': Timeout of 60 seconds was reached
Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :
  download from 'https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable/bin/windows/contrib/4.2/INLA_22.05.07.zip' failed
Warning in install.packages :
  download of package ‘INLA’ failed

Can anyone help me fix it?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Failed to Install INLA
parts:
You need to set the R file download timeout option before running the install.packages() to allow I enough time to download the files. See ?options for some more info.
  options(timeout=10000)
for example.

Finn

messages.author: 9b24b61acd1c2723
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Failed to Install INLA
parts:
Thank you! I had been specifying the timeout option incorrectly. 
Below is the code that ended up working for me, in case any one else has this issue. 

install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"), options(timeout = 10000),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/testing"), dep=TRUE)

On Tuesday, December 27, 2022 at 11:19:14 AM UTC-9 finn.l...@gmail.com wrote:
You need to set the R file download timeout option before running the install.packages() to allow I enough time to download the files. See ?options for some more info.
  options(timeout=10000)
for example.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Failed to Install INLA
parts:
That only works by accident; the options call should _not_ be a part of the repos argument. If that works it’s only because it ends up being run first, and the output of it not breaking the repos argument.

Finn
